features.description: Capability manifest loader + schema validation. Add a small module that discovers `capabilities/*.json`, validates each file against `claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/capability.schema.json`, enforces id == filename stem, and exposes typed read-only models for downstream consumers. This is the foundation that turns ADR-001 from prose into a machine-checkable convention.
steps: Read `capabilities/README.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-001-external-capability-model.md`, and `capability.schema.json`.
Add `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities.py` with `CapabilityManifest`, `CapabilityIndex`, `load_capabilities(root)`, and `validate_capability_file(path)`.
Validation must use the checked-in JSON schema; do not duplicate schema rules by hand beyond id == filename stem and repo-relative setup_doc file existence.
Expose lookup by id and by category. Duplicate IDs fail loud.
Add tests covering valid manifests, missing required field, invalid kind, id/filename mismatch, duplicate ID, missing setup_doc file, and category lookup.
features.acceptance: (1) `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities.py` exists and validates all checked-in manifests. (2) Loader fails loud on invalid schema, duplicate id, filename/id mismatch, and missing setup_doc file. (3) Category and id lookup APIs exist. (4) Tests cover at least 7 cases including all listed failure modes. (5) No external services or credentials required.

evidence_refs.note: F001 manifest loader with typed models, JSON schema validation, id/category lookup, duplicate-id guard, and setup_doc file validation.
Focused F001 test suite: checked-in manifest load, category lookup, valid temp manifest, missing field, invalid kind, filename mismatch, duplicate ID, missing setup_doc, and missing capabilities dir.
Adds jsonschema runtime dependency because manifest validation is now a core loader contract.
Lock-time advisory sidecar emitted when plan status flipped draft to active.

features.description: Doctor/prereq probe binding. Extend existing profile-aware prereq probes so a probe can optionally declare `capability_id`. The doctor output should include the capability ID and setup_doc when a probe is tied to a manifest. This is metadata binding only; the current probe execution behavior and profile severity rules stay unchanged.
steps: Read `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/prereq_registry.py` and current profile tests.
Add optional `capability_id` to `PrereqProbe` and `ProbeResult`.
At registry construction time, validate any non-null capability_id against the F001 loader.
Bind existing relevant probes: Claude CLI -> `agent-claude-cli`, Firebase/gcloud/Firebase target probes -> `firebase-dashboard`, Discord webhook probe -> `discord-notify`.
Ensure JSON output includes capability_id and setup_doc for bound probes while preserving existing fields.
Tests must prove no behavior change to pass/warn/fail/omit decisions.
features.acceptance: (1) PrereqProbe and ProbeResult include optional capability_id. (2) Bound probe IDs validate through the manifest loader. (3) Doctor JSON includes capability_id + setup_doc for bound probes. (4) Existing profile severity behavior is unchanged. (5) Tests cover Claude, Firebase, Discord, and an invalid capability_id registry-authoring failure.

evidence_refs.note: F002 implementation: PrereqProbe/ProbeResult capability_id binding and doctor output metadata.
F002 tests for bound probes, invalid capability ids, setup_doc output, and JSON shape.
Implementer completion envelope.
Auditor signed_off with no findings.
pre_impl auto-cleared and pre_merge operator-approved after signed_off verdict.

features.description: Adapter registry capability_id binding. Extend the local adapter registry so registered adapters can declare which capability manifest they implement. v0 validation is read-only and local: if a registry record includes capability_id, the ID must exist and the adapter category must be compatible with the manifest category. This gives Linear and future adapters one stable link to the manifest convention without adding `dontpanic capabilities` CLI.
steps: Read `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/integrations/adapter_registry.py` and P10/bridge tests.
Add optional `capability_id` to adapter registry records.
Validate capability_id existence through the F001 loader when reading/writing registry records.
For PM-tool adapters, require manifest category `pm-tool` when capability_id is present.
Update Linear fixture/example registry records to use `capability_id: linear`.
Tests cover valid Linear record, missing capability, incompatible category, and backward compatibility for legacy records without capability_id.
features.acceptance: (1) Adapter registry records accept optional capability_id. (2) capability_id validates against manifests. (3) PM-tool adapter category compatibility is enforced. (4) Existing records without capability_id still parse. (5) Linear examples/fixtures use `capability_id: linear`.

features.description: external_refs capability binding. Extend plan external_refs so refs can bind to a capability ID. For v0, PM-tool refs with sync=push_status should resolve to a registered adapter whose capability_id matches the ref capability_id. This keeps external_refs from being freeform service strings while preserving the existing one-way sync behavior.
steps: Read `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/external_refs_sync.py`, plan_loader external ref models, and F002 bridge tests.
Add optional `capability_id` to ExternalRef if not already present through schema/model plumbing.
Validate declared capability_id exists and has compatible category for `kind: pm_issue`.
When resolving a sync target, prefer adapter records matching capability_id; fail loud when sync=push_status and no matching registered adapter exists.
Preserve `sync: none` advisory behavior: missing adapter should not block lock for non-push refs.
Tests cover valid Linear ref, unknown capability, PM ref bound to non-PM capability, push ref with no matching adapter, and sync=none non-blocking behavior.
features.acceptance: (1) ExternalRef supports optional capability_id. (2) PM-tool push refs bind to registered adapters by capability_id. (3) Invalid or incompatible capability IDs fail with actionable errors. (4) sync=none remains non-blocking. (5) Existing external_refs tests remain green.

features.description: Plan-lock advisory required-capabilities sidecar. At `dontpanic plan lock`, inspect the plan's surfaces, external_refs, and matched skill applicability results to infer relevant capability manifests. Emit `evidence/required-capabilities.json` with matched capability IDs, setup_required, setup_doc, owner_boundary summary, and whether each is currently verified/registered. Advisory only: never blocks lock in v0.
steps: Read `plan lock` flow and the skill-applicability sidecar writer.
Add a pure function that computes required/advisory capabilities from plan frontmatter surfaces and external_refs.
Write `evidence/required-capabilities.json` after successful lock, best-effort like applicable-skills sidecar.
Sidecar should include `schema_version`, `plan_id`, `generated_at`, `matches[]`, and `skips[]`.
Matches include capability_id, source (`external_ref|surface|skill`), setup_required, setup_doc, owner_boundary, and current local status (`unknown|verified|missing_config|not_registered`).
Tests cover external_refs -> Linear, surfaces/web+firebase profile -> Firebase advisory, no capability matches -> empty report, and writer failure never blocks lock.
features.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic plan lock` emits advisory `evidence/required-capabilities.json` when capability matches exist. (2) Sidecar includes setup_required, setup_doc, owner_boundary, and current status. (3) Missing optional capabilities do not block lock. (4) Tests cover Linear, Firebase, empty, and failure-is-nonblocking paths. (5) No `dontpanic capabilities` CLI is added.
